title: SC-MT013-SessionScheduling

scope.summary:
GOAL: Cron/scheduling for steerable agent sessions as a Handshake engine capability. The swarm layer already has a scheduler seam (swarm_orchestration/schedule.rs with FR-EVT-SWARM-SCHED-SPINUP-FIRED / SCHED-TEARDOWN-FIRED events, verified in the WP-1 worktree) that spins resources up and down; this MT extends it so OPERATOR-DEFINED SCHEDULES can launch full agent sessions - role injected, task payload composed, workspace bound - on cron expressions, on any lane, vendor-agnostically (Claude and GPT lanes first, future lanes automatically covered because scheduling targets the SC MT-007 session API, never a vendor CLI directly).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/schedule.rs (+ registry storage): SessionSchedule { schedule_id, version, cron_expr (5-field, evaluated in configured timezone), enabled, launch_spec { role_id, task_payload_ref (MT contract ref | prompt ref | none), lane_preference, workspace_mode (worktree|worktree_vm|none), budget }, overlap_policy (Skip|Queue|Concurrent(cap)), misfire_policy (RunOnce|Skip), teardown_policy (max_runtime, idle_timeout), provenance }; PG-backed registry (RO MT-081 registry pattern) with CRUD API + HTTP routes + IPC read; a scheduler loop integrated with the EXISTING swarm schedule seam (extend swarm_orchestration/schedule.rs; do not build a parallel scheduler).

SEMANTICS: fire -> compose launch via RO MT-083 (role + task + workspace) -> spawn via the sanctioned coordinator path (SC MT-007 -> SwarmCoordinator) -> SessionStart hooks fire (SC MT-012, no special path) -> session is a normal steerable session (operator can attach/steer it live). Overlap policy governs the case where the previous scheduled run is still alive (default Skip with typed SKIPPED_OVERLAP event - bounded, HBR-SWARM-001). Misfires (Handshake down at fire time) follow misfire_policy with a typed event either way - never silent. Teardown: max_runtime enforced via supervisor (SC MT-005) graceful stop; every scheduled spawn/skip/misfire/teardown is FR-evented (reuse SCHED-* kinds + RD MT-161 additions where needed) and ledgered.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read swarm_orchestration/schedule.rs in the WP-1 worktree; record its current trigger/teardown model and extend rather than replace (verify the seam names at implementation time against post-merge main).
2. Define SessionSchedule types + hsk.session_schedule@1 JSON schema + PG migration (additive); cron parsing via a maintained crate (e.g. croner/cron - select with a recorded comparison; deterministic next-fire computation, DST-safe in configured timezone).
3. Registry CRUD (API + routes + IPC read) with ledgered mutations, enable/disable, version history.
4. Scheduler loop: tick source integrated with the existing schedule seam; at fire: overlap check -> compose (RO MT-083) -> spawn (SC MT-007) -> record run row linking schedule_id -> session_id.
5. Overlap/misfire/teardown policies implemented + typed events for every non-launch outcome.
6. Tests: cron next-fire correctness incl. DST boundary, overlap Skip/Queue/Concurrent-cap, misfire both policies, teardown max_runtime via fake adapter, schedule->session ledger linkage; live proof: one real scheduled launch on an available lane (or typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF).
acceptance_criteria: hsk.session_schedule@1 registry with CRUD + ledgered mutations; cron next-fire deterministic and DST-safe (tested across a DST boundary).
A fired schedule launches a full session through the sanctioned path: role injected (RO MT-083), workspace bound per workspace_mode, SessionStart hooks fired, session steerable afterwards.
Overlap default Skip produces a typed SKIPPED_OVERLAP event; Queue and Concurrent(cap) behave per spec with bounded concurrency (HBR-SWARM-001).
Misfire handling follows policy with a typed event either way; nothing silent.
max_runtime teardown goes through the supervisor graceful-stop ladder; run rows link schedule_id to session_id in the ledger.
Scheduling targets the session API only - no vendor CLI reference anywhere in the module; the same schedule definition works on two lanes (fake adapter + one real lane, or typed blocker).
The existing swarm schedule seam is extended, not duplicated (no second scheduler loop).
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core session_schedule --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok'
implementation_notes: OPERATOR FRAMING 2026-07-22: cron is an engine capability of the wrapper; schedules must survive vendor swaps because they bind to roles + session API, never to a vendor CLI.
Verify schedule.rs seam names against post-merge main at activation (grounding re-check step in ACTIVATION_READINESS.json).
Cron crate selection: record a short comparison (croner vs cron vs saffron) in research_provenance at implementation; requirement = 5-field cron, timezone-aware, DST-correct next-fire, maintained.
Budget field feeds the same per-parent/budget policy surface as MM MT-106 (scheduled sessions have provenance=schedule, not a parent model session).
No wall-clock sleeps in tests: tick source must be injectable/mockable for determinism.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: API-first registry; scheduled runs appear in the MT lifecycle board (ML MT-125) and audit surface (RD MT-166); dedicated schedule GUI is deferred headroom scope.

target_entries: Dexterity scheduled sessions: cron syntax, overlap/misfire/teardown policies
Linking a schedule to a role and task payload

risk_if_missed: Recurring governed work (nightly validation runs, scheduled maintenance sessions, future self-hosting routines) has no engine-level home and would be improvised per vendor or left manual.

risks: RISK-1: Runaway schedule spawns unbounded concurrent sessions (cost + resource exhaustion).
RISK-2: DST/timezone bugs double-fire or skip fires silently.
RISK-3: A second scheduler loop drifts from the existing swarm scheduler (two sources of truth).
RISK-4: Scheduled sessions bypass policy/consent because no operator is present at fire time.
RISK-5: Misfires after downtime silently drop scheduled work.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): overlap_policy mandatory with bounded Concurrent(cap); coordinator caps still apply; test proves cap enforcement.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): DST-boundary test mandatory; next-fire computation property-tested.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): extend the existing schedule seam; acceptance criterion forbids a parallel loop.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): scheduled launches evaluate the same ToolGate/consent/policy stack; cloud lanes without standing consent produce a typed ConsentRequired outcome, never a silent bypass.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): misfire_policy explicit with typed events; downtime recovery test covers both policies.

research_provenance.source: Operator vendor-agnostic-engine directive 2026-07-22 (cron is a wrapper capability); verified existing seam swarm_orchestration/schedule.rs + FR-EVT-SWARM-SCHED-SPINUP/TEARDOWN-FIRED (WP-1 worktree); RO MT-083 composition + SC MT-007 session API as launch path.
